examples.en: The two countries are cooperating closely.
The team members work while keeping in close contact.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 관계 기관과 긴밀히 상의해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to consult closely with the related agencies on this issue.
I'm contacting you because I have something to discuss in confidence.
The police are working in close coordination with the school.
If departments communicate closely, mistakes decrease.

explain: 협력하다, 연락하다, 소통하다, 상의하다처럼 서로 주고받는 동작과 같이 써요. '가깝게'보다 격식 있어서 업무, 뉴스, 공식적인 말에서 많이 나와요. 형용사 '긴밀하다'는 '긴밀한 관계'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 두 회사가 긴밀히 협력해서 새 제품을 만들었어요.
phrases.en: The two companies cooperated closely to make a new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긴밀히' 뒤에 가장 자주 붙는 동사로, 서로 힘을 합칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 긴밀히, used when parties work together.

phrases.en: I discussed the plan closely with the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 일을 깊이 의논할 때 쓰고, 업무 상황에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when discussing something important in depth, especially at work.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 오래전부터 긴밀한 관계를 유지해 왔어요.
phrases.en: The two have kept a close relationship for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '긴밀히' 대신 형용사 '긴밀하다'를 써서 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form 긴밀하다 modifying a noun, instead of the adverb.

explain_en: It goes with verbs of exchange such as 협력하다 (cooperate), 연락하다 (contact), 소통하다 (communicate) and 상의하다 (consult). It is more formal than '가깝게' and is common in work, news and official talk. The adjective '긴밀하다' is used as in '긴밀한 관계'.

en: important and trivial matters; all sorts of occasions

examples.en: My eldest brother takes care of family affairs.

examples.ko: 부모님은 동네 대소사에 빠지지 않고 참석하세요.
examples.en: My parents never miss neighborhood events.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님이 회사 대소사를 꼼꼼히 챙겨요.
examples.en: The new team leader carefully looks after all the company's matters.
I'm busy every weekend because of relatives' events.

examples.ko: 집안의 대소사가 있을 때마다 온 가족이 모여요.
examples.en: The whole family gathers whenever there's a family occasion.

examples.ko: 결혼이나 장례 같은 대소사에는 꼭 인사를 가야 해요.
examples.en: You must go to pay your respects at occasions like weddings and funerals.

explain: 크고 작은 일을 뜻하고, 특히 결혼·장례·돌잔치 같은 집안이나 모임의 행사를 말할 때 많이 써요. '집안 대소사'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 일상 대화보다는 어른들의 말이나 글에서 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: Grandmother decides all the family occasions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural collocation.

phrases.en: My father takes good care of relatives' big and small events.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식, 장례식 같은 행사를 빠짐없이 돌보는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests attending to weddings, funerals, etc. without fail.

phrases.en: Attending your neighbors' events is good manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이나 행사에 가서 함께한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means going to and joining gatherings and events.

explain_en: It means matters big and small, and is often used for events like weddings, funerals, and first-birthday parties in a family or group. '집안 대소사' is the most natural pairing. It shows up more in adults' speech and writing than in everyday chat.

examples.en: A person from HR also sat in on the interview.
May I join you at dinner?

examples.ko: 회의에 변호사가 동석하면 더 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: It's more reassuring if a lawyer is present at the meeting.

examples.ko: 그 자리에 동석한 분들이 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone who was at that table applauded.
Do you want your parents to be present at the counseling?
I had something to do, so I couldn't join them.

explain: 같은 '자리'에 함께 앉아 있다는 뜻이 중심이라 식사, 회의, 상담 같은 자리에 써요. 식당에서 모르는 사람과 같은 테이블을 쓰는 것은 '합석하다'라고 해요. 탈것을 같이 타는 '동승하다'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: May I sit in on this meeting too?
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락을 구할 때 쓰는 말이고, 더 공손하게는 '동석해도 될까요?'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask permission; a politer form is '동석해도 될까요?'.

phrases.en: Everyone who was present clapped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 자리에 있던 사람들을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the people who were at the same gathering.

phrases.en: The restaurant was crowded, so I shared a table with a stranger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 모르는 사람과 같은 테이블을 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sharing a restaurant table with a stranger.

explain_en: The core idea is being together at the same seat or gathering, so it fits meals, meetings and consultations. Sharing a table with strangers at a restaurant is '합석하다'. Don't confuse it with '동승하다', which is about riding in the same vehicle.

en: each and every one; all faces

examples.ko: 이번 대표팀의 면면을 보면 우승이 기대돼요.
examples.en: Looking at the lineup of this national team, I expect them to win.
The people who attended were really impressive.
The members of the committee have not been made public yet.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들의 면면을 떠올리면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Thinking of each of my classmates makes me smile.

examples.ko: 이 모임의 면면 하나하나가 다 전문가예요.
examples.en: Every single member of this group is an expert.
It's a movie I'm excited for just from seeing the cast.

explain: 여러 사람의 얼굴이나 구성원을 하나하나 가리킬 때 써요. 보통 '대표팀의 면면', '출연진의 면면'처럼 사람 모음 뒤에 붙이고 한 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. '면면히'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: Looking at the participants, I look forward to the competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 구성을 살펴본다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means looking at who the people in a group are.

phrases.en: The members of the judging panel are all impressive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모인 사람들이 모두 뛰어나다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say everyone in the group is outstanding.

phrases.en: The host introduced the members of the cast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모인 사람들을 하나하나 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when presenting the people in a group one by one.

explain_en: It points to the faces or members of a group one by one. It usually follows a group, as in '대표팀의 면면' (the lineup of the national team) or '출연진의 면면' (the cast), and is not used for a single person. It is a different word from '면면히', so don't mix them up.

examples.en: Please keep private chatting to a minimum during the meeting.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 친구와 사담을 나누다가 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded for chatting with a friend during class.

examples.ko: 사담이지만 저는 이 계획이 좀 걱정돼요.
examples.en: This is just between us, but I am a bit worried about this plan.
Can I have a quick private word?

examples.ko: 두 사람은 회의가 끝난 뒤에도 사담을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The two kept talking privately even after the meeting ended.
The private chat went on too long, so the meeting started late.

explain: 회의나 수업, 일하는 자리에서 업무와 상관없는 개인적인 이야기를 가리켜요. '잡담'과 비슷하지만 '사담'은 공적인 자리와 대비해서 쓰는 느낌이 있어요. '사담이지만'은 이야기를 꺼낼 때 앞에 붙이는 말로도 써요.

phrases.en: This is a personal matter, but I'm moving next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인적인 이야기를 꺼내기 전에 앞에 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lead-in said before bringing up something personal.

phrases.en: We chatted privately for a moment before the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일과 상관없는 이야기를 주고받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means exchanging talk unrelated to work.

phrases.en: Please don't chat during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 공적인 자리와 대비하는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but with less sense of contrast to a formal setting.

explain_en: It refers to personal talk unrelated to work in a meeting, class or workplace. It is close to '잡담' (idle chat), but '사담' carries a contrast with the formal setting. '사담이지만' is also used as an opener like 'this is off the record'.

examples.en: My friend suggested that we travel together.

examples.ko: 회사가 저에게 팀장 자리를 제의해 왔어요.
examples.en: The company has offered me a team leader position.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 경기 날짜를 바꾸자고 제의했는데 거절했어요.
examples.en: The other team proposed changing the match date, but we declined.

examples.ko: 제의하는 사람이 먼저 조건을 설명해야 해요.
examples.en: The person making the offer should explain the terms first.

examples.ko: 그에게 먼저 화해를 제의할까 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm wondering whether to offer to make up with him first.
Everyone agreed to the plan he proposed.

explain: 제의하다는 상대에게 어떤 일을 해 보자고 의견이나 안을 내놓을 때 써요. '제안하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '같이 하자고 했어요'처럼 쉬운 말도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My friend suggested that we work together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제의하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 제의하다 and heard more often in daily life.

phrases.en: I received a job offer from a company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제의를 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking from the side of the person who receives the offer.

phrases.en: I politely turned down that offer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 제의를 받아들이지 않을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when you do not accept an offer you received.

explain_en: 제의하다 is for putting an idea or proposal to someone, such as suggesting they do something together. It is close to 제안하다 in meaning. In daily talk people often just say 같이 하자고 했어요.

examples.en: There are four members in our group.
I made the presentation materials with my group members.

examples.ko: 조원 중에 한 명이 아파서 결석했어요.
examples.en: One of the group members was sick and absent.
The group members gathered and divided up the roles.
A new member joined and brightened the mood.

examples.ko: 저희 조원은 모두 열심히 해서 고마워요.
examples.en: I'm grateful that everyone in our group worked hard.

explain: 학교 수업이나 모임에서 여럿이 한 '조'로 묶일 때 그 안의 사람이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '팀원'도 쓰는데 학교에서는 '조원', 회사나 운동에서는 '팀원'이 더 자연스러워요. 숫자 뒤의 '조 원'(trillion won)과는 달라요.

phrases.en: All the group members have gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명의 조원을 함께 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to several group members together.

phrases.en: Minsu and I are in the same group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 조에 속한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who belong to the same group.

phrases.example: 회사에서는 같이 일하는 사람을 팀원이라고 해요.
phrases.en: At a company, people working together are called team members.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조원'과 비슷하지만 회사나 운동에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 조원 but more natural at work or in sports.

explain_en: It is a person in a 조 (group) formed in class or a gathering. 팀원 is similar, but 조원 sounds natural at school and 팀원 at work or in sports. It is unrelated to '조 원' (trillion won) after a number.

examples.en: The meeting opens at ten in the morning.
As soon as the National Assembly opened, a big debate began.
The chair declared the session open, and the meeting began.
Please arrive by 9 so you aren't late for the opening.

examples.ko: 연설자가 개회식에 늦게 도착해서 순서가 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The speaker arrived late to the opening ceremony, so the order changed.

examples.ko: 총회가 예정보다 십 분 늦게 개회했어요.
examples.en: The general meeting opened ten minutes later than planned.

explain: 반대말은 '폐회하다'예요. 회의나 행사가 시작될 때만 쓰는 격식 있는 말이라 '수업을 시작하다'처럼 일상적인 일에는 어울리지 않아요. '개회식', '개회사', '개회 선언'처럼 묶어서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The opening ceremony is held in the auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 행사를 시작하는 공식 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The formal ceremony that starts a meeting or event.

phrases.en: The chairperson declared the session open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 시작한다고 공식적으로 말할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for officially starting a meeting.

phrases.en: The representative gave the opening speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 시작하며 하는 인사말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the speech given at the start of an event.

explain_en: Its opposite is '폐회하다'. It is a formal word used only when a meeting or event begins, so it doesn't fit everyday things like starting a class. It often appears in compounds such as '개회식', '개회사' and '개회 선언'.

dis.h: formally open a meeting or session

p.n: The passive needs a subject marked with 가/이, so the same object sentence does not work.

examples.en: An accident happened, so an emergency meeting was held.
The team leader suddenly called an emergency meeting.
I couldn't eat lunch because of the emergency meeting.
I was late for my appointment because I attended an emergency meeting.
The emergency meeting ended in an hour.
Today's schedule all changed because of the emergency meeting.

explain: 갑자기 생긴 급한 일 때문에 여는 회의예요. '긴급회의를 열다', '긴급회의를 소집하다'처럼 쓰고, 회사와 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 회사는 내일 아침 긴급회의를 열기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The company decided to hold an emergency meeting tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 시작하거나 하기로 정할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for holding a meeting.

phrases.en: All the team leaders attended the emergency meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에 가서 함께한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to go and take part in the meeting.

phrases.example: 지금 긴급회의 중이라 전화를 못 받아요.
phrases.en: I'm in an emergency meeting now, so I can't answer the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 회의가 진행되는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the meeting is going on right now.

explain_en: It is a meeting held because of a sudden urgent matter. It is used as '긴급회의를 열다' or '긴급회의를 소집하다' and appears often at work and in the news.

examples.en: The union members held a rally in front of the company.
I joined the union as a member last year.
Most of the union members voted in favor of the strike.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 새 노조원을 환영하는 모임이 있어요.
examples.en: This weekend there is a gathering to welcome new union members.

examples.ko: 노조원에게는 여러 가지 복지 혜택이 있어요.
examples.en: Union members get various welfare benefits.
My friend, who is a union member, went to vote.

explain: '노동조합'을 줄인 '노조'에 사람을 뜻하는 '원'이 붙은 말이에요. 같은 사람을 '조합원'이라고도 해요. 회사 직원 전체가 아니라 노조에 가입한 사람만 가리키니까 '직원'과 구분해서 써요.

phrases.en: I am a union member at this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노조원'을 문장 끝에 넣어 자신이나 다른 사람의 신분을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite sentence ending that states someone's status as a union member.

phrases.en: The union members gathered and had a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 노조에 가입한 여러 사람을 함께 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' refers to several union members as a group.

phrases.example: 우리 회사 조합원은 백 명이 넘어요.
phrases.en: Our company has more than a hundred union members.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노조원'과 같은 사람을 가리키는 비슷한 말이에요. '조합원'은 노조 외의 다른 조합 회원에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym for the same person; '조합원' can also refer to members of other kinds of associations.

explain_en: It is '노조' (short for 노동조합, labor union) plus '원' (member). The same person is also called a '조합원'. It refers only to those who joined the union, not to all employees, so keep it separate from '직원'.

examples.en: A new plan is being discussed at the meeting.
That issue was discussed for a long time yesterday.
The budget will be discussed next week.

examples.ko: 논의되는 내용은 모두 메일로 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: I will send you everything that is discussed by email.
We decided after the opinions were fully discussed.
Several methods were discussed, so it is hard to choose.

explain: 안건이나 문제가 주어이고, 회의나 공식적인 자리에서 이야기가 오갈 때 써요. 친구끼리 편하게 이야기하는 일에는 잘 쓰지 않고, 그때는 '이야기하다'를 써요. 사람이 하면 '논의하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 문제는 지금 회의에서 논의되고 있어요.
phrases.en: That issue is being discussed in the meeting now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 이야기가 오가는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the discussion is going on right now.

phrases.en: That topic hasn't been discussed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 다루지 않았다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it hasn't been covered yet.

phrases.en: It will be discussed again at the next meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a future plan.

explain_en: The subject is an agenda item or issue that is being talked over in a meeting or formal setting. For casual chats between friends use '이야기하다' instead. When a person does it, it is '논의하다'.

p.n: 토론되다 suggests debate with differing views.

examples.en: We discussed next week's schedule.
They are discussing the budget issue in the meeting.

examples.ko: 이 일은 가족과 먼저 논의해 보세요.
examples.en: Talk this over with your family first.
There is too much to discuss.
After a long discussion, we made a decision.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 따로 만나서 논의하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I'd like the two teams to meet separately and discuss it.

explain: '이야기하다'보다 격식 있고, 결정을 내리려고 의견을 나눈다는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 논의하다', '~와/과 논의하다'로 써요. 친구와 수다를 떨 때는 쓰지 않고, 회의·직장·학교 발표에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Let's discuss this problem together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'는 한번 해 본다는 뜻이에요. 회의에서 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-a/eo boda' means to give something a try. Use it to suggest something in a meeting.

phrases.en: This matter needs more discussion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 결정하기 전이라 이야기가 더 필요하다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a decision is not made yet and more talk is needed.

phrases.en: I discussed moving with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '논의하다'보다 덜 딱딱해요. 가족이나 친구와 일상적인 일을 이야기할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is less stiff than '논의하다'. You can use it with family or friends about everyday matters.

explain_en: It is more formal than '이야기하다' and suggests exchanging opinions in order to reach a decision. Use '~을/를 논의하다' or '~와/과 논의하다'. It is not for chatting with friends; it fits meetings, work, and school presentations.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 단과대가 열 개 있어요.
examples.en: Our university has ten colleges.

examples.ko: 공대는 이공 계열 단과대 중에서 가장 커요.
examples.en: The engineering college is the biggest of the science and engineering colleges.
Each college has its own student council.

examples.ko: 단과대 건물이 멀어서 수업 사이에 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The college buildings are far apart, so I run around between classes.

examples.ko: 경영대는 우리 학교에서 인기 있는 단과대예요.
examples.en: The business college is a popular college at our school.
Each college holds its own welcome party for new students.

explain: 한 대학교 안에 있는 큰 단위로, 공과대학, 인문대학, 경영대학 같은 것이에요. 보통 '공대', '인문대'처럼 줄여서 말해요. 단과대 아래에 여러 학과가 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling goes to the engineering college.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공과대학'을 줄여서 말하는 단과대 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short name for the engineering college, one kind of 단과대.

phrases.en: The college's students are preparing the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 단과대에 속한 학생들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for students belonging to a single college.

phrases.example: 우리 단과대 건물은 정문 옆에 있어요.
phrases.en: Our college building is next to the main gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단과대가 쓰는 건물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the building that a college uses.

explain_en: It is a large unit within one university, such as the college of engineering, humanities or business. People usually shorten the names, like '공대' and '인문대'. Several departments sit under each college.

examples.en: The interview requires the presence of someone from HR.
If you'd like to sit in, please tell us in advance.

examples.ko: 상담할 때 보호자 동석은 선택 사항이에요.
examples.en: A guardian being present during counseling is optional.

examples.ko: 동석 여부를 알려 주시면 자리를 준비할게요.
examples.en: If you let me know whether you'll join us, I'll prepare a seat.
I got a request to join them, so I stopped by briefly to say hello.

examples.ko: 회의에 동석 가능한 인원은 두 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only two people can sit in on the meeting.

explain: 모임, 식사, 상담, 회의처럼 같은 자리에 함께 있는 것을 말해요. '동석 여부', '동석 가능'처럼 안내문이나 공지에 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '같이 앉다', '자리를 함께하다'라고 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.example: 보호자 동석 가능이라고 안내문에 적혀 있어요.
phrases.en: The notice says a guardian may sit in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 함께 있어도 된다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on notices to mean someone may be present too.

phrases.en: Please let us know in advance whether you will attend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같이 참석하는지 아닌지를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask whether someone will be present or not.

phrases.en: There are three people sitting in altogether.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 함께 있던 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who was present at the gathering.

explain_en: It means being at the same gathering, meal, consultation or meeting together. It often appears in notices as '동석 여부' or '동석 가능'. In daily talk people spell it out as '같이 앉다' or '자리를 함께하다'.
